Internal class for a binary SBM fit under the double-standard sampling design (MNAR, depending on the value of each dyad).

Source: R/R6Class-simpleSBM_fit.R
SimpleSBM_fit_MNAR.Rd

The missing dyads are integrated out given the blocks. A dyad between blocks q and l is missing with probability \(m_{ql} = \pi_{ql}(1 - p_1) + (1 - \pi_{ql})(1 - p_0)\), where \((p_0, p_1)\) are the parameters of the sampling: the update of the blocks gets the term \(\sum_{j} \sum_l \tau_{jl} \log m_{ql}\) over the missing dyads (i, j). The missing dyads tie the connectivity to \((p_0, p_1)\): the M-step maximizes over the three jointly, by EM on the missing dyads (the posterior probability that a missing dyad between blocks q and l is an edge is \(\nu_{ql} = \pi_{ql}(1 - p_1) / m_{ql}\)), iterated to convergence, all in Q x Q given the memberships.

It is not designed to be called directly by the user.

SimpleSBM_fit_MNAR$update_parameters()

update parameters estimation (M-step)

Usage

SimpleSBM_fit_MNAR$update_parameters(psi = NULL, tol = 1e-08, maxit = 10000)

Arguments

psi

the parameters (p0, p1) of the sampling, starting point of the joint M-step. If NULL, or with a single block (where the sampling is constrained to dyad sampling), the SBM is fitted on the observed dyads.

tol, maxit

tolerance on the parameters and maximal number of iterations of the EM on the missing dyads

Returns

invisibly, the updated (p0, p1), or NULL if the SBM is fitted on the observed dyads

SimpleSBM_fit_MNAR$update_blocks()

update variational estimation of blocks (VE-step)

Usage

SimpleSBM_fit_MNAR$update_blocks(log_lambda = 0)

Arguments

log_lambda

Q x Q matrix, the log-probability that a dyad between blocks q and l is missing (field log_lambda of doubleStandardSampling_fit)

SimpleSBM_fit_MNAR$polish_log_tau()

for each node, the log-likelihood of the observed data it would contribute to each class if hard-assigned there (parameters held fixed), used to decide node-swap moves in missSBM_fit$polish().

Usage

SimpleSBM_fit_MNAR$polish_log_tau(log_lambda = 0, ...)

Arguments

log_lambda

Q x Q matrix, the log-probability that a dyad between blocks q and l is missing

...

additional arguments, not used

Returns

an N x Q matrix
